findings.checklist_item: Extend the throughput floor (and either the retry or an explicit out-of-scope note) to `_ensure_blobs_present`'s `--refetch --no-filter` fetch — and state whether `_materialize_tree`'s lazy fetch is in scope — so no whole-repo remote fetch on the materialization path is left bounded only by the 300s ceiling.
evidence: `_ensure_blobs_present` builds `["fetch", "--no-filter", "--refetch", "--quiet", remote, "--end-of-options", sha]` and calls `subprocess.run(..., timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` at 300s (repo_snapshot.py:534-543)
It is a full-blob transfer ('~2 hours on a 25k-file tree' if lazy) — the same cold-clone workload the plan's evidence table exercises ('cold full clones of the whole 80 MB repo')
The plan's extraction list names `_fetch_origin` but not `_ensure_blobs_present`, and Scope's low-speed args are described only for 'the snapshot fetch'
`_materialize_tree` env comment (repo_snapshot.py:554) notes it 'can drive git's own (lazy) network fetch' — also unbounded by throughput
findings.finding: The plan's fix targets only `_fetch_origin`, but `_ensure_blobs_present` (repo_snapshot.py:512-545) is a second whole-repo remote fetch (`git fetch --no-filter --refetch`) on the same materialization path, bounded only by `_GIT_TIMEOUT=300` with no throughput floor; a stall there still burns 300s.
scenarios: A cold materialization whose resolution fetch left blobs missing (`_has_missing_blobs` True) then stalls inside `_ensure_blobs_present` — the low-speed abort never applies and the review burns the full 300s
findings.suggested_fix: Move `_ensure_blobs_present` into `git_fetch.py` alongside `_fetch_origin` and apply the same `-c http.lowSpeedLimit -c http.lowSpeedTime` args to its argv; if you deliberately exclude it (best-effort, no retry), say so explicitly in Scope with the rationale that it is `_has_missing_blobs`-gated and rare.

findings.checklist_item: State how retained callers (`_materialize_tree`, `_ensure_blobs_present`) reach `_git`/`_has_remote` after the move and preserve the `repo_snapshot._git` monkeypatch seam that test_snapshot_blobless_747f depends on.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:560 `read = _git(repo_root, "read-tree", sha, env=env)` inside `_materialize_tree` (a function NOT in the moved cluster)
tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py:223-234 patches `rs._git` and asserts `_materialize_tree` passed the env
Plan: the git-subprocess cluster "moves whole ... no behaviour moves with it"
findings.finding: Moving `_git` into `git_fetch.py` breaks a monkeypatch seam relied on by a RETAINED caller. `_materialize_tree` (repo_snapshot.py:560) — which the plan leaves in `repo_snapshot.py` — calls `_git`, and `tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py:230` monkeypatches `rs._git` specifically to intercept that call (asserting `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`). After the move, `_materialize_tree` would call `git_fetch._git` (a different binding), so patching `rs._git` no longer intercepts it and the test's `seen` list stays empty. The plan's 'no behaviour moves with it' claim omits this call-graph coupling between the moved `_git` and retained callers.
scenarios: Post-extraction, `_materialize_tree`/`_ensure_blobs_present` (retained) invoke `git_fetch._git`; a test or operator patch on `repo_snapshot._git` no longer takes effect.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-point the leaf's parent from epic 061c (LLM provider seam) to bug df2c-e4b8-496d-4698, which explicitly delegated the http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime stall-abort scope to this child — so the leaf's What/Scope/ACs sit under a containing contract that actually contains them.
evidence: Leaf parent_id resolves to 061c-ecd1-8967-4a76 = 'LLM provider seam — first-class Bedrock + best-effort OpenAI-compatible, with tiered verdict provenance'; df2c is linked as relation 'discovered_from', not parent.

Epic 061c Scope enumerates only src/rebar/llm/{runner,anthropic_model,structured,config,parity}.py, plan_review/sidecar.py, completion_sidecar.py, pyproject.toml, infra/terraform, docs — no src/rebar/_snapshot/ path; its ACs are all provider-seam/Bedrock/provenance.

Leaf Scope: 'src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py (new — extracted plumbing + the stall abort and retry)' and 'src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py' — a subsystem disjoint from the epic's src/rebar/llm/* domain (dir listing: cache.py, janitor.py, repo_snapshot.py).

df2c (final/closed state) states: 'Acceptance criterion 5 (configure http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime so the stall aborts in seconds) is out of scope here and is filed as a separate child ticket' and its close comment: 'Child 12e4-8c74-a738-4014 (abort a stalled git fetch...) is UNAFFECTED and still worth doing.'
findings.finding: The leaf's declared scope (a throughput-keyed git-fetch stall abort + bounded retry in a new src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py, extracted from repo_snapshot.py) is not a subset of its DECLARED parent epic 061c-ecd1-8967-4a76, whose plan and every acceptance criterion are confined to the LLM provider seam (src/rebar/llm/*, Bedrock/OpenAI-compatible providers, verdict provenance tiers, parity, terraform/IAM). The epic's plan contains nothing about the _snapshot git-fetch plumbing, so the leaf delivers work the parent's plan does not contain. The leaf's substantive contract actually lives in bug df2c-e4b8-496d-4698 (linked only as `discovered_from`), whose plan explicitly carved out this exact work as its former AC5 and named this child (12e4) as the ticket that would deliver it.
findings.location: Leaf ticket 12e4 parent linkage (parent_id=061c-ecd1-8967-4a76) vs. Scope section ('src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py', 'repo_snapshot.py')
scenarios: Epic 061c's AC 'every child story is closed' would gate the provider-seam epic's completion on unrelated git-fetch work, and conversely the git-fetch task inherits a provider-seam containing contract that neither authorizes nor bounds it.
A reviewer checking the leaf against its declared parent finds no covering scope, obscuring that df2c is the real contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Change 12e4's parent to df2c-e4b8-496d-4698 (its `discovered_from` source, whose former AC5 is this leaf's scope). If the operator intends 061c to remain the umbrella, add the git-fetch/snapshot-reliability scope to the epic's plan first so the leaf becomes a genuine subset (parent-wins realignment), which will also re-stale and force re-review of the epic's attestation.
